Dinitrophenol is a protonophore, meaning it transports protons across membranes. It is hydrophobic in both its protonated and deprotonated forms, and is therefore able to pass through the inner mitochondrial membrane in either form. It carries protons across the membrane, dissipating the proton gradient. This means that the electron transport chain is no longer inhibited and therefore operates at a maximal rate. This results in an increased rate of O2 consumption.  A - There is more heat produced due to the increased rate of ATP synthesis is incorrect. There is more heat produced due to the increased rate of electron transport chain activity, which is due to the dissipation of the proton gradient.  C - The rate of NAD/NADH turnover is reduced is incorrect. The rate of NAD/NADH turnover is increased as the electron transport chain is operating at a maximal rate.  D - Thermogenin channels sense the loss of proton gradient and stimulate release of fatty acids is incorrect. Thermogenin channels sense the loss of proton gradient and stimulate the release of stored fat for use as fuel.  E - The rate of fuel consumption is only increased in brown adipose tissue is incorrect. The rate of fuel consumption is increased in all tissues, as the electron transport chain is operating at a maximal rate.
